name: claw-cli
description: CLI client for the nClaw AI assistant: prompt, chat, pairing, keys, memories, topics, sessions, MCP server, OpenAI-compatible proxy, and schema migrations.
author: nself

actions.prompt: Send a single prompt and get a response
actions.pair: Generate a pairing code for nClaw clients
actions.unlock: Temporarily unlock the web UI for setup
actions.mcp: Start an MCP server for AI tools

notes: Named 'claw-cli' (not 'claw') to avoid colliding with the existing paid backend service plugin registered as 'claw' in plugins-pro/registry.json (plugins-pro/paid/claw, the ɳClaw bundle). binaryName is explicitly overridden to 'nself-claw' since internal/plugin.ProxyCommand resolves nself-<cmdName>, keyed on the top-level command word the user types ('claw'), not the plugin's registry name. This IS the Three-Surface Model in action: this plugin is the thin, unlicensed CLI client (App tier, always free per doctrine) for the paid ɳClaw backend (Backend tier) — the CLI commands have zero license checks in the moved source, matching the ai-studio/gateway/gauth/model precedent from the same extraction batch. Extracted from cli/cmd/commands/claw*.go and cli/internal/claw/* under CLI-R11. cli/internal/config (7239 lines, the full .env cascade + schema + defaults) is unreachable from this module; claw_migrate.go and claw_pair.go only ever read six specific env vars off it, so those six fields were reimplemented directly as internal/projectenv (see its doc comment) rather than duplicating the whole package. internal/claw/migrations/ (SQL files) was carried over verbatim for parity, though in practice clawMigrationsDir() reaches this plugin's own copy only via the relative dev-mode fallback paths — the primary 'installed plugin' path it checks (~/.nself/plugins/claw/migrations) is the PAID backend's own installation directory, unchanged by this extraction.
